classes.name: Captain
classes.description: You lead from the front with a loyal cohort and a pouch of battle dice. Maneuvers keep the whole line pointed the same way.

features.name: Battle Tactics
features.description:
You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called Battle Dice.

Battle Dice. You have two Battle Dice, which are d6s. A Battle Die is expended when you use it. You regain all expended Battle Dice when you roll Initiative or finish a Short or Long Rest. Your Battle Die changes and more Battle Dice become available as shown on the Battle Dice column of the Captain Features table.

Maneuvers. You can expend Battle Dice to perform maneuvers. Your maneuver options are detailed later in the class description.

Saving Throws. If a maneuver requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Strength or Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.description:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Lances and Longswords.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: Cohort
features.description:
You gain a loyal Cohort who carries your banner and follows your lead.

Initiating a Cohort. Choose your Cohort's stat block from those listed later in the class description. Following an 8-hour initiation period, which can be done during a Long Rest, that creature becomes your Cohort until you initiate a new Cohort to replace it. You can have only one Cohort at a time.

Cohort in Combat. Your Cohort is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands. In combat, your Cohort takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). Your Cohort uses your Charisma for its attack and damage rolls.

Cohort Save DC. If your Cohort forces a creature to make a saving throw, the DC is 8 plus your Charisma modifier and your Proficiency bonus.

Features. Your Cohort improves and gains new features when you reach certain Captain levels, as shown on the Captain Features table.

Proficiencies. Your Cohort has proficiency in skills and saving throws listed in its statistics. Your Cohort uses your Proficiency Bonus instead of its own. Because Cohort statistics already include a +2 Proficiency Bonus, you need only adjust skill and saving throw proficiencies starting at level 5.

Cohort Spells. Throughout your adventure, you may wish to customize the spells listed in a Cohort's stat block. You can exchange one of the spells listed in the Spellcasting feature with another of the same level. Your GM decides if a spell is appropriate for a Cohort. Generally, the Priest's spells are from the Cleric spell list, the Mage's spells are from the Wizard spell list, and the Shaman's spells are from the Druid spell list.

features.name: Cohort Species
features.description: When you initiate a new Humanoid Cohort, you can also give it one of the following traits to reflect its species.

options.name: Dragonborn: Draconic Ancestry
options.description: The Cohort has Resistance to one of the following types of damage associated with its dragon progenitor (Captain's choice): Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison.

options.name: Dwarf: Resistances and Immunities
options.description: The Cohort has Resistance to Poison damage and Immunity to the Poisoned condition.

options.name: Elf: Fey Ancestry
options.description: The Cohort has Advantage on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

options.name: Gnome: Saving Throws
options.description: The Cohort has proficiency in one of the following saving throws: Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.

options.name: Goliath: Powerful Build
options.description: The Cohort has Advantage on any ability check it makes to end the Grappled condition. It also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

options.name: Halfling: Brave
options.description: The Cohort has Advantage on saving throws it makes to avoid or end the Frightened condition.

options.name: Human: Skillful
options.description: The Cohort has proficiency with one skill of your choice.

options.name: Orc: Relentless (1/Day)
options.description: When the Cohort is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it is reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

options.name: Tiefling: Fiendish Ancestry
options.description: The Cohort has Resistance to one of the following types of damage associated with its fiendish progenitor (Captain's choice): Fire, Necrotic, or Poison.

features.name: Legendary Commander
features.description:
Immediately after another creature's turn, you can choose yourself or an ally within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you to take a Legendary Action. This action is one of the following: Attack (one attack only), Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Magic (cast one cantrip only), or Utilize. A creature can only take one Legendary Action each round. When a creature takes the Dash or Disengage action in this way, the benefits of that action last until the end of the creature's next turn.

You can use this feature to take three Legendary Actions and regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Counter-Shot [Maneuver]
features.description: When an enemy you can see hits a creature with a ranged attack roll, you can take a Reaction and expend one Battle Die to attempt to intercept the attack. You must be holding a Ranged weapon and the creature must be within your weapon's range to use this maneuver. Subtract the Battle Die from the attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.

features.name: Hundred-Arrow Volley
features.description:
When you take the Attack action with a Ranged weapon, you can replace one of your attacks with a flurry of projectiles in one of the following ways.

Arrow Rain. Choose a point within your weapon's range. You launch several projectiles that rain down in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder centered on that point. Make a separate ranged attack roll against each target in that Cylinder.

Scatter Shot. You launch several projectiles in a 20-foot Cone. Make a separate ranged attack roll against each target in that Cone.

features.description: Your elegant swordplay puts enemies where you want them. Whenever you hit a creature of Large size or smaller with a Melee weapon, you can force the target to move to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it, and you can move 5 feet. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

features.name: Dirty Tactics
features.description:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Melee weapon, you can use one of the following effects.

Flank. Your Cohort has Advantage on the next melee attack roll it makes against the target while you are within 5 feet of it before the end of your next turn.

Pocket Sand. The target has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of your next turn.

Trip. The target has the Prone condition if it is Large or smaller.

features.name: All Hands on Deck
features.description:
At your directive, your crew works in perfect unison. As a Bonus Action, you can issue a series of directives to allies within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. Each ally has Advantage on the next D20 test it makes before the start of your next turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

creatures.name: Cohort
creatures.description:
You gain a loyal Cohort who carries your banner and follows your lead.

Initiating a Cohort. Choose your Cohort's stat block from those listed later in the class description. Following an 8-hour initiation period, which can be done during a Long Rest, that creature becomes your Cohort until you initiate a new Cohort to replace it. You can have only one Cohort at a time.

Cohort in Combat. Your Cohort is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands. In combat, your Cohort takes its turn immediately before or after your turn each round (your choice). Your Cohort uses your Charisma for its attack and damage rolls.

Cohort Save DC. If your Cohort forces a creature to make a saving throw, the DC is 8 plus your Charisma modifier and your Proficiency bonus.

Features. Your Cohort improves and gains new features when you reach certain Captain levels, as shown on the Captain Features table.

Proficiencies. Your Cohort has proficiency in skills and saving throws listed in its statistics. Your Cohort uses your Proficiency Bonus instead of its own. Because Cohort statistics already include a +2 Proficiency Bonus, you need only adjust skill and saving throw proficiencies starting at level 5.

Cohort Spells. Throughout your adventure, you may wish to customize the spells listed in a Cohort's stat block. You can exchange one of the spells listed in the Spellcasting feature with another of the same level. Your GM decides if a spell is appropriate for a Cohort. Generally, the Priest's spells are from the Cleric spell list, the Mage's spells are from the Wizard spell list, and the Shaman's spells are from the Druid spell list.

class_resources.name: Battle Dice
class_resources.description: A pool of d6s (growing to d8s) spent to fuel maneuvers. You regain all expended Battle Dice when you roll Initiative or finish a Short or Long Rest.

abilities.name: Bolster
abilities.description: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Battle Die to motivate an ally within 60 feet of yourself. The next time your ally makes an attack before the start of your next turn, it adds the Battle Die to the attack and damage roll.
abilities.execution: Bonus Action, expend one Battle Die

abilities.name: Born Leader
abilities.description: When you fail a Wisdom or Charisma check, you can expend one Battle Die to add it to the roll, potentially turning it into a success. You can only use this maneuver once per turn.
abilities.execution: When you fail a Wisdom or Charisma check, expend one Battle Die

abilities.name: Morale Boost
abilities.description: When an ally you can see within 60 feet of yourself fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to expend one Battle Die and add it to the roll, potentially turning it into a success.
abilities.execution: Reaction, expend one Battle Die, when an ally fails a save

abilities.name: Rally
abilities.description: As a Bonus Action on your turn, you can expend one Battle Die to choose one ally within 60 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. That creature regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled + your Charisma modifier.
abilities.execution: Bonus Action, expend one Battle Die

abilities.name: Staggering Strike
abilities.description: When you hit a creature with an attack using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend one Battle Die as a Bonus Action to daze the target. Add the Battle Die to the attack's damage roll.
abilities.execution: Bonus Action, expend one Battle Die, when you hit

abilities.name: Eagle Eye [Maneuver]
abilities.description: Once per turn when you miss with a ranged attack roll, you can expend one Battle Die and add it to the attack roll, potentially causing the attack to hit.

abilities.name: Counter-Shot [Maneuver]
abilities.description: When an enemy you can see hits a creature with a ranged attack roll, you can take a Reaction and expend one Battle Die to attempt to intercept the attack. You must be holding a Ranged weapon and the creature must be within your weapon's range to use this maneuver. Subtract the Battle Die from the attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.

abilities.name: Skirmish [Maneuver]
abilities.description: When you make an attack using a weapon, you can expend one Battle Die as a Bonus Action to make an attack using the same weapon or a different one later on the same turn. One attack must be a melee attack roll and the other must be a ranged attack roll.

abilities.name: Challenge [Maneuver]
abilities.description: When you hit a creature with an attack using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend one Battle Die as a Bonus Action to goad the target into attacking you. Add the Battle Die to the attack's damage roll. Until the start of your next turn, the target has Disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you while you are within 5 feet of the target.

abilities.name: High Morale
abilities.description: You can use your Morale Boost maneuver when two or more creatures, including yourself, simultaneously fail a saving throw against the same effect, such as a dragon's breath weapon. Each creature that failed its saving throw gains the benefit of Morale Boost, and you only expend one Battle Die.
